accepted.s: After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly performed which of the following functions?
o: It functioned only as the provincial legislature of the newly formed Union
It functioned as the legislature of British India under the control of the Viceroy
It functioned only as the constitution-making body until 26 January 1950
It functioned both as a sovereign constitution-making body and as the Dominion legislature
accepted.x: The Act made the Constituent Assembly fully sovereign in its constitution-making role and also made it the Dominion legislature. The Central Legislative Assembly consequently ceased to function.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Assembly’s dual constitutional and legislative roles.
accepted.sec: Constituent Assembly's dual role after the Act  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly when it functioned as the constitution-making body and who presided over it as the legislature, respectively?
o: G.V. Mavalankar and Dr Rajendra Prasad
Dr B.R. Ambedkar and G.V. Mavalankar
Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr Rajendra Prasad
Dr Rajendra Prasad and G.V. Mavalankar
accepted.x: Dr Rajendra Prasad chaired the Assembly in its constitution-making capacity, whereas G.V. Mavalankar presided over it when it functioned as the legislature.
accepted.tq: Separate similar institutional roles by matching each role with its presiding officer.
accepted.sec: Constituent Assembly's dual role after the Act  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The strength of the Constituent Assembly declined from 389 to 299 primarily because
o: the nominated members resigned before the commencement of the Constitution
members representing the areas that became part of Pakistan withdrew from the Assembly
the British Government dissolved the provincial representation
the princely states refused to send their representatives
accepted.x: The representatives from the territories that went to Pakistan withdrew from the Constituent Assembly, reducing its strength from 389 to 299.
accepted.tq: Identify the direct cause of an institutional numerical change.
accepted.sec: Constituent Assembly's dual role after the Act  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Constituent Assembly continued after 26 January 1950 as the
accepted.x: After the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, the Constituent Assembly functioned as the Provisional Parliament until the first general elections held in 1951–52.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional transition sequence to identify the successor institution.
accepted.sec: Constituent Assembly's dual role after the Act  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Radcliffe Boundary Commissions:
1. Separate Boundary Commissions were constituted for Punjab and Bengal.
2. Both the Commissions were chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
3. Sir Cyril Radcliffe was an Indian civil servant with long experience of provincial administration in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Separate Commissions were formed for Punjab and Bengal, and both were chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe. Radcliffe was a British lawyer with little knowledge of India, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong biographical description while retaining the correct commission facts.
accepted.sec: Radcliffe Boundary Commissions - provinces and chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Sir Cyril Radcliffe, who chaired both the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions, was primarily a
o: member of the Indian Civil Service
accepted.x: Sir Cyril Radcliffe was a British lawyer who had little knowledge of India when he was appointed to chair both Boundary Commissions.
accepted.tq: Test the person’s professional identity rather than the office held.
accepted.sec: Radcliffe Boundary Commissions - provinces and chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission award was ready on 12 August 1947 but was published on
accepted.x: The award was ready on 12 August 1947 but was published on 17 August 1947. The delayed publication was intended to avoid Britain being blamed for the violence associated with partition.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date on which a decision was ready from the date on which it was published.
accepted.sec: Radcliffe Boundary Commissions - provinces and chairman  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the work period of the Constituent Assembly?
o: 3 years, 1 month and 18 days; 12 sessions and 175 sitting days
2 years, 9 months and 18 days; 10 sessions and 160 sitting days
2 years, 11 months and 18 days; 11 sessions and 165 sitting days
2 years, 11 months and 8 days; 11 sessions and 150 sitting days
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, held 11 sessions and sat for 165 days.
accepted.tq: Match a cluster of closely related duration and session figures.
accepted.sec: Time taken - years, sessions, sitting days  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For how many days was the Draft Constitution considered by the Constituent Assembly?
accepted.x: The Draft Constitution was considered for 114 days. The figure of 141 days refers to the sittings of the Drafting Committee, not to the Assembly’s consideration of the Draft.
accepted.tq: Separate two nearby numerical figures belonging to different stages of constitution-making.
accepted.sec: Time taken - years, sessions, sitting days  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly sat for how many days?
accepted.x: The Drafting Committee sat for 141 days. This is distinct from the 114 days during which the Draft Constitution was considered by the Assembly.
accepted.tq: Use institutional attribution to distinguish similar duration figures.
accepted.sec: Time taken - years, sessions, sitting days  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the preparation of the Indian Constitution:
1. The framers consulted the constitutions of about 60 countries.
2. Approximately Rs 64 lakh was spent on the constitution-making process.
3. The Draft Constitution initially contained 395 Articles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The framers consulted the constitutions of about 60 countries and the expenditure was about Rs 64 lakh. The Draft contained 315 Articles; 395 Articles belonged to the adopted text, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-stage numerical trap involving the Draft and the adopted Constitution.
accepted.sec: Time taken - years, sessions, sitting days  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the Draft Constitution with the adopted Constitution?
o: The Draft had 395 Articles, whereas the adopted text had 315 Articles.
The Draft had 315 Articles and the adopted text had 470 Articles.
The Draft had 315 Articles, whereas the adopted text had 395 Articles.
Both the Draft and the adopted text had 395 Articles.
accepted.x: The Draft Constitution contained 315 Articles. The Constitution as adopted contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
accepted.tq: Compare figures belonging to successive versions instead of treating them as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: Time taken - years, sessions, sitting days  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Linguistic Provinces Commission was appointed by the Constituent Assembly on
accepted.x: The Linguistic Provinces Commission, also known as the Dhar or Dar Commission, was appointed by the Constituent Assembly on 17 June 1948.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the later Draft and JVP dates.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Linguistic Provinces Commission appointed in 1948?
accepted.x: The Commission consisted of S.K. Dhar, Dr Pannalal and Jagat Narayan Lal. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a member of the later JVP Committee.
accepted.tq: Find the person belonging to the neighbouring committee rather than the named body.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Linguistic Provinces Commission rejected linguistic reorganisation and instead gave importance to
o: administrative convenience, economic viability, geography and national unity
religious majority, princely privileges, military necessity and language purity
population alone, historical boundaries, caste composition and trade routes
provincial autonomy, separate electorates, cultural uniformity and judicial independence
accepted.x: The Commission rejected linguistic reorganisation as the basis and favoured administrative convenience, economic viability, geographical considerations and national unity.
accepted.tq: Select the complete set of criteria associated with the Commission’s recommendation.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The JVP Committee was constituted in December 1948 by the
accepted.x: The JVP Committee was constituted by the Congress in December 1948. Its members were Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who constituted the body?’ test to distinguish two related committees.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Committee)
A. Linguistic Provinces Commission
B. JVP Committee
C. Radcliffe Boundary Commission
D. Drafting Committee

List-II (Association)
1. Constituent Assembly
2. Indian National Congress
3. Punjab and Bengal boundaries
4. Constitution-making process

option_a: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4
option_b: A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4
option_c: A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3
option_d: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3

accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional associations and eliminate the swapped codes.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The report of the JVP Committee, submitted in April 1949,
o: rejected linguistic reorganisation for the time being but left room for Andhra if there was strong public demand
immediately recommended the creation of all linguistic States
recommended that Andhra be merged permanently with Tamil Nadu
accepted only the reorganisation of Punjab and Bengal
accepted.x: The JVP Committee also rejected linguistic reorganisation for the time being. However, it left room for the creation of Andhra if there was strong public demand.
accepted.tq: Identify the qualified recommendation rather than an absolute acceptance or rejection.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra in the Draft Constitution:
1. Andhra was included in the First Schedule of the Draft.
2. Andhra was dropped from the Draft published on 21 February 1948.
3. The deletion followed objections from Tamil and Kannada areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra was initially in the First Schedule of the Draft, but it was omitted from the Draft published on 21 February 1948 after Tamil and Kannada objections.
accepted.tq: Check the complete sequence of inclusion, deletion, date and cause.
accepted.sec: Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dar) and JVP Committee  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Jawaharlal Nehru accepted the demand for a separate Andhra on
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru accepted the Andhra demand on 27 November 1947. The later Andhra State was formed in 1953 after the continuing linguistic-State demand.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of political acceptance from the date of State formation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Before Indian independence, the Madras Assembly had resolved to divide the Presidency into which four units?
accepted.x: The Madras Assembly resolved to divide the Presidency into Andhra, Tamil, Karnataka and Kerala four months before independence.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete four-part geographical list without substituting later State names.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The immediate historical significance of the Indian Independence Act, 1947 was that it
o: ended provincial autonomy and restored direct British rule over India
combined sovereignty with partition and enabled a quick transfer of power under dominion status
abolished the Constituent Assembly and transferred power to the princely States
created a unitary republic with universal adult franchise
accepted.x: The Act gave sovereignty to India in the context of partition. Congress accepted dominion status to facilitate a quick and peaceful transfer of power and to support a strong Centre.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines the Act’s constitutional consequence with its political context.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following offices in chronological order according to the sequence associated with the transfer of power:
A. Last Viceroy of India
B. First Governor-General of independent India
C. Last Governor-General of India

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and also the first Governor-General of independent India. C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General, giving the sequence A, B, C.
accepted.tq: Use the first/last distinction to place overlapping offices in sequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Last Viceroy of India — C. Rajagopalachari
Last Governor-General of India — C. Rajagopalachari
First Governor-General of independent India — Lord Mountbatten
Last Viceroy of India — Lord Mountbatten
accepted.x: C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General, not the last Viceroy. Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and the first Governor-General of independent India.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped office-holder in a first/last comparison.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee?
o: The Dhar Commission accepted linguistic States, whereas the JVP Committee rejected them.
The Dhar Commission dealt with boundaries, whereas the JVP Committee dealt exclusively with the national anthem.
Both accepted linguistic reorganisation without qualification.
Both rejected linguistic States for the time being, though the JVP Committee left room for Andhra in case of strong public demand.
accepted.x: Both bodies turned down linguistic reorganisation at that stage. The JVP Committee nevertheless left open the possibility of Andhra if public demand became sufficiently strong.
accepted.tq: Compare the common conclusion while preserving the important qualification.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The continuing demand for a separate Andhra ultimately resulted in the creation of Andhra State in
accepted.x: The Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee rejected linguistic States at the time, but the Andhra demand continued and resulted in the Andhra State of 1953.
accepted.tq: Connect an earlier committee recommendation with the later political outcome.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of national symbols:
1. Article 51A(a) refers to respect for the National Flag and the National Anthem.
2. Article 51A(a) expressly names the National Song along with the Flag and the Anthem.
3. The 2026 amendment to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act extended to the National Song statutory protection comparable to that of the Anthem.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 51A(a) names the National Flag and the National Anthem, not the National Song. The 2026 amendment gave the National Song, including Vande Mataram, statutory protection comparable to that of the Anthem.
accepted.tq: Catch the precise-word trap between the National Anthem and the National Song.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The debate surrounding statutory protection for Vande Mataram has been linked with which of the following?
o: The Objective Resolution of 13 December 1946 and Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
The Constituent Assembly’s statement of 24 January 1950 and Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986)
The Radcliffe Award of 17 August 1947 and Minerva Mills (1980)
The JVP Report of April 1949 and S.R. Bommai (1994)
accepted.x: The debate has been connected with the Constituent Assembly’s statement of 24 January 1950 and the Supreme Court decision in Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986).
accepted.tq: Match a current constitutional debate with its specific historical and judicial reference points.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
